text:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: Elevated 5xx and gateway timeouts detected for /v1/generate (region: eu-west-1). p95 latency ~1.2s -> 6.8s, p99 ~18s. Error rate 5xx increased from 0.1% -> 3.7% in last 5m. Paging oncall: jamie (oncall).

jamie (oncall): on it — jumping into dashboards now. any deploys around the window?

sam: I'm seeing a canary deploy at 2025-11-14T17:42:10Z for tag release/2025.11.14-canary. metrics show a sharp tail in kvcache hit ratio dropping, a lot of repeated full model loads.

maria: +1, also seeing increased gateway timeouts from the edge LB to infer nodes. trace ids clustered around node subset id i-0a3b.

jamie (oncall): can we pin the deploy window? who promoted canary -> traffic?

sam: auto-rollout to 10% at 17:45 UTC, we have rollout policy: canary -> 10% after 3m health checks.

maria: logs (snippet):
```
2025-11-14T17:46:03Z ERROR inferer: kvcache miss, loading model shard 7 took 3.1s
2025-11-14T17:46:04Z WARN  runtime: kernel fallback for quantized matmul, exec time 2.4s
2025-11-14T17:46:05Z ERROR http: upstream timeout to inferer i-0a3b status 524
```

jamie (oncall): this looks like a regression in the canary that increases cold loads and kernel fallback path latency. high impact on p99. We need immediate mitigation: roll the canary back to previous stable. anyone on deploy?

deploy-bot: Deployment 2025.11.14-canary promoted to 10% at 17:45:12Z by rollout-controller.

ops-runner: I can kick a rollback. executing safe rollback to tag release/2025.11.13-stable now. running:
```
redwood deploy rollback --service inference-api --to release/2025.11.13-stable --reason "p99 latency regression in canary" --non-interactive
```

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated by ops-runner. Canary traffic draining, routing back to stable.

sam: watching p95/p99 in realtime — p95 dropping from 6.8s -> 1.5s already at 17:47:40Z. p99 still elevated but trending down.

maria: gateway 524s decreasing, error rate trending toward baseline. good sign.

deploy-bot: Rollback completed. Traffic fully on release/2025.11.13-stable at 17:48:12Z.

jamie (oncall): confirmed: post-rollback p95=0.98s, p99=1.6s, 5xx down to 0.2%. Marking incident as mitigated. :white_check_mark:

product-support: We had 12 customer errors flagged by monitors (mostly http 524). Which customers saw increased errors? we need list for outreach.

sam: pulling request logs now. customer-impact query:
```
select customer_id, count(*) from access_logs
where path = '/v1/generate' and status >= 500 and ts between '2025-11-14T17:42:00Z' and '2025-11-14T17:50:00Z'
group by customer_id order by count desc limit 50;
```

sam: top impacted customers: cust-204 (56 errors), cust-17 (22), cust-88 (9). most errors concentrated in eu-west-1.

product-support: thanks. I'll draft outbound notes for the top affected customers. escalate to enterprise CS for cust-204.

jamie (oncall): next steps / actions:
- rollback confirmed and mitigation successful
- assign postmortem owner: maria (eng-runtime)
- collect artifacts: deploy diffs, kernel selection logs, kvcache metrics, canary config
- consider stricter canary validation (longer health window for heavy seq workloads)

maria: I will own the postmortem. I'll collect the following: canary manifest, commit diff, runtime logs, perf traces. ETA draft: EOD tomorrow.

ops-runner: note: the canary changed quantization kernel selection thresholds (PR #4821). suspect kernel fallback for quantized matmuls on older GPU types. adding to investigation.

jamie (oncall): slack handoff: I'm handing oncall to sarah at 18:00 UTC — sarah, please monitor paging for 30m and confirm stability.

sarah: acknowledged — monitoring for 30m and will reopen if regressions reappear.

jamie (oncall): for the postmortem, include customer impact assessment (list + timeframe), rollout gating gaps, and remediation plan (fix kernel selection or revert heuristics).

maria: will include recommended mitigations: explicit model warmup in canary, increase canary delay to 10m for kernel-path sensitive releases, and add a p99 SLA smoke test pre-promote.

product-support: I'll queue the customer notifications after we have draft postmortem and mitigation summary.

jamie (oncall): closing thread for now — mitigated and rollback complete. reopening if any alerts bubble up. :lock:
